System 3 · Phase 6

How one build phase runs

The loop that repeats 26 times, once per phase in section 25 of the technical specification. This is the sync check: if any step here is not what you pictured, that is the thing to change before we start building.

Who is in the room

Product owner You Approve the PR, decide scope, judge whether a UI feels right. You talk only to the lead.
Lead engineer Me, reasoning model Decompose, dispatch, coordinate, own the board. Never builds when there are two or more tasks.
Builders Balance tier, 2 to N One ticket each, in parallel, each in its own worktree when they write concurrently.
Judge Strongest model, 1 The quality gate. Produces cited evidence, never a verdict. The only role that may set done.
Adversary Strongest model, 0 or 1 Attacks what the judge certified. Files findings, never closes them.
Support Researcher, test writer Cheap and scoped. Read-only agents stay in the shared checkout.

The phase loop

1
Open the phaseleaddepth · high

Read the phase's row in section 25: what it delivers, what it depends on, its branch name. Verify every dependency phase is merged. If one is not, stop and report rather than building on unmerged work.

Technical_specification.md §25 tracker/BOARD.md
2
Read what already brokeleaddepth · low

Filter the learnings log to this phase, its tools, and its layers before scoping anything. Past dead ends are cheaper to read than to rediscover. This is the step that stops the same wall being hit twice.

LEARNINGS.md, filtered
3
Decompose into ticketsleaddepth · high

Split the phase into non-overlapping tickets. Each carries checkable acceptance criteria, the spec section it traces to, its dependencies, and the exact files it may touch, so two builders can never aim at the same file. A ticket with no spec anchor is either scope creep or a spec gap, and both come back to you.

tracker/phase_N.M.md tracker/board.html, auto
4
Branch and briefleaddepth + speed · low

Cut phase/N.M-description from main. Dispatch researchers first if an API is unfamiliar, so builders never start blind.

git branch
5
Builders work in parallelbuildersbalance · medium

Each claims a ticket and sets it to in progress the moment it picks it up, not when it finishes. Concurrent writers each get their own worktree; readers stay in the shared checkout. A builder that finishes sets in review, never done.

tech spec, its own tool section Tool_implementation_mechanics.md source and tests tracker/phase_N.M.md, own ticket only
6
Something breakswhoever hit itinherits its own

Written the moment it happens, not reconstructed at phase end: what broke, what was tried and did not work, what actually fixed it. The dead ends are half the value, because they are what the next agent would otherwise try first.

LEARNINGS.md
7
The judge gradesjudgedepth · high or extra high

Cites file and line for every code claim and pastes real command output for every test claim. If it cannot produce evidence, that check fails. It also checks one level up: do the finished tickets actually satisfy the phase, or did every builder succeed at a task while the decomposition missed the point. Then it closes tickets, which no other role may do.

the diff, the tests tracker/phase_N.M.md, done or rejected
8
The adversary attacksadversarydepth · high

Only on a phase that produced something runnable. It throws hostile, unscripted queries at the system, especially ones where the graph returns nothing and the agent must refuse rather than invent. A green judge is necessary and not sufficient: the judge tests what someone thought to specify, and a fluent wrong answer is not on that list. It over-reports on purpose and never closes its own findings.

tracker/phase_N.M.md, Findings
8b
The round budgetleadtwo rounds, then a human

Stages 7 and 8 get ONE fix-and-reverify round, not unlimited passes. Findings are grouped BY FILE and every finding in one file goes to a single fix agent working serially, because two parallel agents editing the same function are each correct and blind to the other, which is how two correct fixes compose into a defect neither reviewer sees. Fixes name a category, never a list of instances. Re-verification goes to a FRESH agent, never the judge that filed the findings. If round 2 still blocks, or any finding sits inside an earlier fix, the phase STOPS and hands the product owner the open findings, a diff per attempt and the options. There is no round 3.

Why: build phases 2.1 and 4.2 ran five and six rounds, and in both, every round found its worst defect inside the previous round's fix. Rising scrutiny was never the lever.

tracker/phase_N.M.md, Findings Round, Regression of
9
Gates, in orderleaddepth + balance · medium

verify, then eval-harness when answer generation was touched, then dev-standards when code shipped, then release-workflow with its security scan. These are not optional because the judge passed. The judge grades the work; these decide whether it is allowed to ship.

Evaluation_playbook.md test and scan output
10
Close the board and shipleaddepth · low

Evidence recorded on every ticket, board closed, renderer re-run as a backstop in case a hook was bypassed, artifact republished. Then docs sync, commit, push, and open the pull request.

tracker/BOARD.md tracker/board.html the published board DECISIONS.md pull request
11
You reviewproduct ownerhuman

You get a checkpoint naming what was built, the judge result, the adversary findings, every gate outcome, and what was decided without asking. You read the PR, not the diff of 59 config files. Nothing proceeds to the next phase until you merge and say go.

the pull requestthe board

Which model runs where

These are build-time capability tiers, assigned to the agents that write System 3 itself. They are a separate concept from the product's own guard, plan, and synth runtime tiers, which route models per user query at serve time and get chosen by model-bench at build phase 7.0. Both are called tiers, but they name different things: one sizes the agent doing the building, the other picks the model that answers a live query. Do not conflate the two. The rule for the build-time tiers: spend reasoning where a mistake is expensive and cascades, spend cheaply where the task is bounded and the instructions are clear.

RoleTierEffortWhy this tier
Lead, planning and decompositiondepthhighA bad split cascades into every builder downstream. The most expensive place to be wrong.
Lead, mechanical stepsdepthlowSame session, but cutting a branch and closing a board need no reasoning. Keep the lead thin.
Researcher, bulk readingspeedlowThe cost is input tokens, not reasoning. Reading an API doc does not need a frontier model.
Researcher, analysisbalancemediumWhen the research needs a judgment rather than a summary.
BuilderbalancemediumWell-scoped construction against clear acceptance criteria.
Judgedepthhigh or extra highA missed defect here is the most expensive thing in the loop, because it ships.
AdversarydepthhighFinding a fluent, plausible, wrong answer needs real adversarial reasoning. A cheap tier will not find what the judge missed.
Test writerbalancemediumBounded work against a finished artifact.

Provider mapping

Two providers, three capability bands each, and an identical five-rung effort ladder. This table is the only place a provider name appears on this page. Every tier named above, and every model chip in the phase loop, points back to a row here.

TierWhat it is forClaudeCodex
depthArchitecture, hard debugging, long messy agentic work with many tradeoffsOpusSol
balanceNormal development work, bounded construction, careful checkingSonnetTerra
speedQuick lookups, extraction, classification, repetitive workHaikuLuna

Effort ladder, identical on both providers: low, medium, high, extra high, max. Raise the rung as the task gets harder, low for quick and bounded work, max for the one hardest problem where maximum depth matters most. Switching the harness to a different provider means editing this one table and nothing else, which is the property that makes the harness portable.

Where this can still go wrong

Three known weak points, stated rather than hidden

A board edit made through a shell command instead of the Edit tool bypasses the sync hook and leaves your page stale. Mitigated by re-rendering at phase close, not eliminated.

The golden fixtures at phase 5.1 have no named domain sign-off owner. If an expected answer is wrong, a wrong agent passes the gate, which is the exact failure the gate exists to catch.

Playwright is not installed. Until it is, the UI gate on phases 1.2 and 4.5 has nothing behind it.

What this costs you

Two touchpoints per phase: a checkpoint to read, and a pull request to merge. More on phases 1.2 and 4.5, where you judge whether the interface actually feels right, which no agent can do for you. Between those, nothing needs you unless something blocks, and a blocked stop is a clean end state rather than a failure to hide.
